Trump stands by Howard Lutnick despite commerce secretary dismissing warning about Nvidia Chinese spy affair
See more of our coverage in your search results.
WASHINGTON — President Trump stood by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick Friday amid questions about the department’s handling of Nvidia chip sales following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang.
“I have not lost confidence. He’s a different kind of a guy,” the president said of Lutnick during a White House news conference before praising his underling as a “very good businessman.”
Lutnick has come under fire following revelations that his Commerce Department declined to bar Megaspeed from purchasing Nvidia AI chips over suspicions the Singapore-based company was smuggling them to China.
Advertisement
Additionally, US intelligence reportedly had warned Trump that Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive engaged in an extramarital affair with Jensen Huang (no relation), could be a Chinese spy.
Trump acknowledged Lutnick was not a traditional cabinet pick like Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent who the president described as “out of central casting.”
But Lutnick, Trump insisted, “has a natural business instinct.”
Advertisement
Bessent claimed last week that Treasury and several other departments favored blacklisting Megaspeed, but faced inaction by Lutnick’s agency.
“Commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC Nov. 13. “You … have to ask them about their internal processes.”
Both men joined President Trump on his trip to Asia this week, with Lutnick getting a ride back to the White House from Joint Base Andrews on board Marine One Thursday night.
Advertisement
Native New Yorkers, Trump and Lutnick are longtime friends who share a love of sports and a history of moving through the city’s social circles.
But Lutnick also has close ties to Jensen Huang, who described the commerce secretary as his closest friend in the administration and said he spoke to him often.
When President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, his Cantor Fitzgerald firm held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.
Advertisement
The firm is now run by Lutnick’s sons, Brandon and Kyle. Its Nvidia share count fell by nearly half between September 2025 and March 2026, a CNBC analysis found.
Here’s the latest on the Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy:

- Nvidia’s accounting practices are focus of probe by Wall Street regulators: report
- Jensen Huang’s cruel employee insults included ‘abortion’ quip, threat to ‘pee on your brain’: report
During the same period, the Commerce secretary faced pressure from administration officials to address suspected smuggling of Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China via Megaspeed.
Meanwhile, Jensen Huang was lobbying administration officials to open up sales of Nvidia’s chips, including to China.
Advertisement
The investigation into whether or not Megaspeed sent chips to China was removed from Commerce late last year and turned over to the Justice Department after Nvidia’s general counsel contacted investigators at the former department to ask for an update.

sources.news_title: Trump Backs Lutnick After Senator’s Criticism of Chip Smuggling
Trump: I Have Not Lost Confidence in Lutnick
Trump says he still backs Lutnick, urges Nvidia's Huang to apologize
Trump says he still has confidence in Lutnick
sources.text:
President Donald Trump on Friday said he has not lost confidence in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, pushing back on growing pressure from bipartisan lawmakers and even members of his own administration.
Trump, at a wide-ranging White House press conference, was asked about Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., telling The Wall Street Journal that, if Lutnick is to be ousted, it should happen soon enough for the Republican-led Senate to confirm his replacement before Democrats take over the chamber.
"Well, Tom's right," Trump replied, saying he would agree with taking swift action if he had indeed lost confidence in Lutnick. "But I have not lost confidence," Trump said in response to a question from CNBC's Eamon Javers.
"He's a different kind of a guy, very good businessman. He's not traditional," Trump said, praising Lutnick's involvement in the U.S. taking an equity stake in Intel.
